messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected: inference_streaming_p99 > 1500ms (now 1800ms) in shared-gpu-pool-us-east-1.
Alert link: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/alerts/INC-1799991000
Affected routes: /v1/generate (streaming). Estimated affected customers: 3 tenants, traffic spike from tenant-42.

maya: I'm oncall and paged. @aj can you take lead on root cause? Paging via phone as well.

aj: taking it. pulling metrics now. p95=420ms p99=1800ms. streaming stalls count increased from ~5/min to ~180/min. Queue length on inference-router up to 1200.

aj: checking GPU metrics and node IO. nvidia-smi snapshot:
```
GPU 0 Temp 82C Util 93% Mem 91%
Processes:
  pid 24512 tenant-42 model: redwood/large-v1  98% GPU mem
```

aj: node iostat showing heavy nvme write waits:
```
Device:         tps    kB_read/s    kB_wrtn/s    await
nvme0n1        324.00      120.0       10240.0     221.3
```

maya: smells like noisy neighbor - tenant-42 causing high IO and saturating GPU/mem leading to KV cache eviction and streaming stalls. Let's isolate.

aj: checking cgroup for container 24512. blkio stats:
```
/sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/24512/blkio.throttle.io_service_bytes  read: 1.2TB write: 12.4TB
```

maya: mitigation plan (short):
- throttle blkio for tenant-42 to reduce IO.
- apply CPU/GPU memory limits if still necessary.
- route high-QPS customers from affected tenants to smaller model fallback (redwood-model-small-v2) and enable prefix-caching.
- if unstable, evacuate tenant to dedicated-pool-2 and schedule node reboot after low traffic window.
- notify CS and impacted customers.

aj: applying immediate throttle. command:
```
echo "nvme0n1 2020" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/24512/blkio.throttle.read_iops_device
echo "nvme0n1 15000" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/24512/blkio.throttle.write_iops_device
```

aj: throttle applied. within 60s p99 dropped to ~720ms, p95 unchanged ~430ms. streaming stalls reduced to ~30/min.

maya: good. please also reduce batch sizes on the router for that tenant to minimize KV pressure: set `max_batch_tokens`  to 128 for tenant-42 route.

aj: done. routing change pushed to canary: `/routes/tenant-42` now points to smaller batch and fallback model for streaming. curl test:
```
# baseline test to streaming endpoint
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOK" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood/large-v1","stream":true,"input":".."}' | ts
# observed chunk latencies: 50-120ms
```

eli: CS update: impacted customers: Acme Corp (tenant-42), Zephyrus Apps (tenant-88 intermittent), BetaLabs (tenant-99 small error spike). Acme reported degraded response during morning window. They need an ETA for full remediation.

maya: TL;DR for CS: we throttled tenant IO which reduced p99 significantly and removed most stalls. Next steps: move Acme (tenant-42) to dedicated-pool-2 overnight and run soak for 2 hours, follow up with root cause hygiene. ETA to complete migration: 4h if no blockers. I'll coordinate with infra.

sanjay: picking up handoff. Summary: noisy neighbor (tenant-42) IO saturated nvme causing GPU mem/KV thrashing -> p99 & stream stalls. Mitigations in place: blkio throttle, reduced batch size, fallback model routing. Current status: p99 ~600-750ms, stalls ~25/min, error rates back to baseline. Actions for next shift:
- schedule tenant migration to dedicated-pool-2 (infra ticket #INF-5043)
- run disk health check and NVMe SMART on node
- follow up with model team on long-running kernel causing heavy write patterns
- create postmortem and update noisy-neighbor runbook with cgroup commands + thresholds.

sanjay: leaving this in maya's hands for immediate notifications; I'll take ownership of migration and the postmortem doc. tagging @eli for CS follow-up.

eli: thanks. we'll notify Acme with interim mitigation note and let them know we expect migration complete in 4h window.

incident-bot: INCIDENT NOTE: mitigations applied and partial recovery observed. Status set to MONITORED. Please update when fully resolved or if escalation needed.
